## GET verification (Meta webhook handshake)

- The **verify token never appears as a plain parameter** -- it lives only in the 'Verify Token' crypto credential, used as an HMAC key.
- Verification compares a precomputed HMAC **commitment** (HMAC of the token using itself, computed once at setup time with `scripts/generate_webhook_verify_commitment.py`) against an HMAC of the incoming token computed the same way at request time. The commitment is a one-way function of the token, but it is still deterministic -- it does not by itself protect a low-entropy token from offline guessing. Use only a token with at least 256 bits of entropy (the setup script generates one).
- This workflow ships with an **unconfigured placeholder** in `EXPECTED_COMMITMENT` in the 'Evaluate GET Verification' node and **fails closed**: every GET request is rejected until you replace it with your own valid 64-character lowercase hex commitment. See the documentation for exact setup steps.
- This workflow's settings disable execution-data persistence for this trigger (see the Settings tab), but Meta still sends `hub.verify_token` in the callback URL's query string -- your reverse proxy, load balancer, CDN, or APM tooling may log it independently of n8n. See the documentation's "Infrastructure logging risk" section before deploying.

## POST signature verification

- Requires the Webhook trigger's **Raw Body** option (already enabled) -- signatures are computed over the exact bytes Meta sent, never a re-parsed/re-serialized copy.
- The **app secret never appears as a plain parameter** -- it lives only in the 'App Secret' crypto credential, used as an HMAC key by the Crypto node.
- Comparison is constant-time (no data-dependent early exit) to reduce timing side-channel risk.
- Rejected requests **never reach the verified branch** -- the IF node gates it structurally.
- The verified branch never echoes the customer payload back in the HTTP response -- attach your downstream processing at the marked NoOp node; do not add customer data to the response.
- This workflow's settings disable execution-data persistence for successful, failed, and manual runs (see the Settings tab). Physical removal from n8n's database happens on n8n's normal background pruning schedule (bounded, not instantaneous -- see the documentation), not the instant a request completes.
- **Replay/deduplication is NOT implemented here** -- add your own if needed.
- This gateway does not claim protection against a compromised app secret, and does not track message history. It has been verified as a template against a specific n8n version and test suite (see the documentation) -- it is not a certified production security product.
